subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion
central_question: How can standard measurement, reference points and patterns of movement help us describe length, position and motion accurately?
in_scope_units: How we measure — body-based units, number and unit, and the need for standardisation
Standard units — SI unit of length and the relations among kilometre, metre, centimetre and millimetre
Correct measurement — selecting a suitable device, placing the scale, eye position and using a broken scale
Measuring curved lines with flexible tape or thread
Describing position using a fixed reference point
Moving things — deciding motion or rest relative to a reference point and time
Linear motion along a straight path
Circular motion along a circular path
Oscillatory motion to and fro about a fixed position
Periodic nature of repeated circular and oscillatory motion

known_pitfalls.claim: Handspan is a reliable standard unit for everyone.
known_pitfalls.correction: Handspans vary from person to person, so measurements of the same object can differ.

known_pitfalls.claim: A measurement is complete when only the number is written.
known_pitfalls.correction: A measurement must contain both a number and a unit.

known_pitfalls.claim: A broken scale cannot be used.
known_pitfalls.correction: An object can start at another clear mark, and its length is the final reading minus the initial reading.

known_pitfalls.claim: An object is either always at rest or always in motion.
known_pitfalls.correction: Motion and rest depend on whether position changes with time relative to a chosen reference point.

recommended_example_progression: Explain why handspan measurements differ and why standard units are needed.
Practise correct scale reading and measurement with a broken end.
Measure a curved line with thread.
Establish reference point, motion and rest using the bus-passenger and kilometre-stone examples.
Classify linear, circular and oscillatory motion.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Refer to the chapter-end section 'Let us enhance our learning', Questions 1-13, followed by the 'Learning further' activities.
